architecture:
Use case: scientific-educational. Generate one polished scientific system architecture diagram for an English research paper on ordinary mobile crowdsensing. Wide landscape, approximately 3:2, white background, flat vector-like linework, restrained blue and orange, legible black sans-serif text, generous whitespace, no photo, no 3D, no vehicles, no decorative scenery, no figure number or caption. Every label must be exactly spelled. The diagram is a conceptual architecture, not experimental data.
Two large clearly separated zones: LEFT "CLIENT DEVICE" and RIGHT "PLATFORM / ADVERSARY". Dashed vertical boundary labeled "Observation boundary".
In LEFT, upper box "Local sensing" with small secondary text "True location stays local". A downward arrow leads to box "Eligibility + availability". Another left-zone box "Public-history belief" points to box "BSP participation gate"; label this arrow "Predicted belief". The gate points to Eligibility + availability with label "Gate probability q". Include a short annotation inside LEFT: "Gate depends on public history, not true location". The eligibility box outputs to a smaller box "Common deadline release".
In RIGHT, upper box "Normal tasks + adaptive probes". A clear arrow traveling from that right box across the boundary into LEFT to Eligibility + availability, labeled "Task region and deadline". Lower RIGHT box "Bayesian inference" with small secondary text "Linkable account history". Exactly one output arrow crosses left-to-right from Common deadline release into Bayesian inference, labeled "Report or silence". A loop arrow wholly in RIGHT from Bayesian inference back to Normal tasks + adaptive probes is labeled "Choose next probe". A smaller annotation inside RIGHT reads "No true location, delivery status, or gate coin". A thin return arrow from the public Report or silence line to the LEFT Public-history belief represents belief update and is labeled "Public outcome update". Avoid any direct arrow from Local sensing or true location across the observation boundary. No equations beyond q. Keep all arrows unambiguous and avoid intersections. Output high-resolution print-friendly diagram.
method:
Use case: scientific-educational. Create a high-resolution journal-quality method diagram for "Branch-safe participation (BSP)", ordinary mobile crowdsensing. White background, flat vector-like design, blue and orange accents, precise black sans-serif type, no vehicles, no photography, no invented performance charts. Landscape, two panels separated by a faint vertical line, generous spacing and clear arrowheads, no overall caption or figure number. Labels must be spelled exactly.
LEFT PANEL label "(a) Filtering one task". Top rounded box "Public belief + task region" with smaller "Predict from public history". Arrow down to diamond "Report posterior within cap?". Diamond's right branch labelled "No" leads to orange box "Set q = 0". Down branch labelled "Yes" leads to blue box "Choose largest q allowed by silence". Both branches join at a box "Attempt truthful completion" with smaller line "Inside region + available + gate passes". This box leads down to "At the deadline: report or silence". This leads down to "Update belief from observed outcome". A simple return loop from this final box to the top box is labelled "Next task". Short footer below this panel: "Check both possible outcomes before participating".
RIGHT PANEL label "(b) Why silence matters". Display an illustrative four-cell strip: three blue outlined cells labelled "0.2", "0.2", "0.2" and one orange outlined cell labelled "0.4". Above first three cells bracket label "Task region"; fourth cell label "Outside". Above strip small text "Prior belief". Beneath strip write exactly "Availability = 0.9; cap = 0.4". Then two clearly separate arrows down:
left arrow label "Report" goes to blue outlined result box containing "Largest posterior = 1/3" and line "Within cap".
right arrow label "Silence" goes to orange outlined result box containing "Outside posterior = 0.4 / 0.46" and a larger line "= 0.870 > 0.4".
Under these result boxes one orange emphasis line "A success-only check misses this leak".
Bottom-right footer: "Illustrative calculation with q = 1".
Scientific constraints: the numbers are an exact analytical example, not measured experimental results. The gate uses public belief only, never true location to choose q. True location is used only for eligibility. Avoid any arrow implying future location is observed. Prefer minimal journal typography, not marketing graphics.
